rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pilgrimage to the Kaaba uniquely invites all people into Islam because Jews and Christians did not perform it.
rows.anchor: هذه العبادة الوحيدة التي لم تكن عند أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer, fasting, and almsgiving were shared with earlier religious communities, so commands to perform them would not uniquely call people to Islam.
rows.anchor: الصلاة الصيام والزكاة الديانات مشتركة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh already prayed at the Kaaba, albeit by whistling and clapping, so a command to pray would not distinguish Islam as pilgrimage does.
rows.anchor: وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl is broad and may be intentional or accidental; it can describe an animal losing its way, unlike ghawāya.
rows.anchor: الضلالة قد تكون عن قصد أو عن غير قصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawāya is deliberate persistence in error, applies to morally responsible people, and contrasts with sound judgment, while ḍalāl contrasts with guidance.
rows.anchor: أما الغواية فهي عن قصد وهو الإمعان في الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad “your companion” recalls his long life among them and their knowledge of his honesty, undermining accusations of deviation or madness.
rows.anchor: فيهم عمراً طويلاً وخالطهم وعاشرهم وعرفوا صدقه وأمانته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “your companion” occurs in three Quranic passages, each denying madness or deviation of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وردت صاحبكم في ثلاث مواضع في القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath evokes falling; deviation is a moral fall, “in” misguidance suggests falling, and guidance “upon” suggests elevation and firm footing.
rows.anchor: ولو لاحظنا القسم في بداية السورة هو دلالة على الهوي والسقوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first sent two messengers; after the people rejected them, He supported them with a third rather than sending all three at once.
rows.anchor: أرسل رسولين أول مرة فكذبهما القوم فقوّاهما تعالى برسول ثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “we strengthened” means the mission and call were strengthened, rather than the two messengers personally.
rows.anchor: التعزيز ليس للرسل أنفسهم وإنما التعزيز يكون للدعوة التي يدعو الرسل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting faith is graver than neglecting prayer: a believer who is lax in worship may repent and be forgiven, and does not thereby leave the faith.
rows.anchor: أما إذا كان مؤمناً وتكاسل في الطاعات هذا تُرجى له التوبة والمغفرة ولا يخرج من المِلّة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “لك” to the first warning and omitting it from the second matches the stronger threat to disbelief and signals that the two failings differ in gravity.
rows.anchor: فذكر (لك) ومقابل (ولا صلّى) قال (فأولى) بحذف (لك) إشارة إلى عظم الإيمان وأهميته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out because it is the most important act of worship.
rows.anchor: فلأن الصلاة هي أهم العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later “denied and turned away” restates the lack of belief and prayer; each is reinforced and receives its own warning, yielding four threats.
rows.anchor: وجاء (كذّب) مقابل (لا صدّق) و (تولّى) مقابل (لا صلّى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran describes failure to judge by revelation as kufr, injustice, or sinfulness; the author lists the descriptions as injustice, sinfulness, then kufr.
rows.anchor: ترتيب الصفات: الظلم ثم الفسق ثم الكفر

words: مَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every failure to rule by revelation is necessarily disbelief: favoritism may make the judge unjust without taking him outside the faith, though every case falls under one of the three descriptions.
rows.anchor: ليس بالضرورة أن يكون الكفر هو الذي دعاه لعدم الحكم، هل أراد أن يحابي أحداً؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruler who departs from the prescribed retaliation judgment to favor someone is an oppressor; this example shows why the motive need not be disbelief.
rows.anchor: الحاكم حكم محاباة لشخص لا يكون كافراً ولكنه يكون ظالماً

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: The accusative “الصابئين” coordinates with another accusative; grammarians parse nominative “الصابئون” either by the position of إنّ’s noun or as a new clause.
rows.anchor: النصب ليس فيه إشكال وإنما الرفع هو الذي كثيراً ما يُسأل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative leaves the Sabians outside إنّ’s emphasis because the author regards them as farther astray and lower in religious standing than the named scriptural communities.
rows.anchor: (إنّ) تفيد التوكيد معناه أنه قسم مؤكّد وقسم غير مؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ṣabaʾ means leaving a faith or religion; the Sabians are described as having departed from the recognized religions.
rows.anchor: صبأ في اللغة أي خرج عن المِلّة، عن الدين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents two Sabian groups: star worshippers and followers of John; unlike the other named communities, they are generally said to lack a scripture, though some claim they have one.
rows.anchor: وهم قسمان وقسم قالوا إنهم يعبدون النجوم وقسم متبعون ليحيى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Mu’minun the questions concern ownership, so the answer uses the possessive lām in “لله.”
rows.anchor: السياق في آية المؤمنون كان في السؤال عن الملكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Ra‘d the question is who the Lord is, focusing on divine oneness rather than ownership, so the answer is “Allah.”
rows.anchor: فالسياق في مقام التوحيد وليس في مقام الملكية وإنما عن الذات الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse, “أنزل” means “created.”
rows.anchor: (أنزل) في هذه الآية بمعنى خلق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In linguistic usage, idnāʾ means drawing near and letting the garment fall or drape to cover the body from top to bottom.
rows.anchor: الإدناء هو الإرخاء والإسدال، ما ستر الجسم كله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jilbāb linguistically means a covering garment, whether worn over another garment or understood as the garment worn over clothes.
rows.anchor: الجلباب في اللغة هو ما يستر من الملابس سواء فوق الثوب أو الثوب

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Some linguists define the jilbāb specifically as any garment a woman wears over her other clothes.
rows.anchor: وقسم يقول هو كل ثوب تلبسه المرأة فوق الثياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically, khimār is a head covering and jayb is the chest opening; he explicitly limits this explanation to language, not jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: الخمار هو غطاء الرأس، والجيب هو فتحة الصدر. هذا في حدود اللغة وليس من الناحية الفقهية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single soul is Adam and the spouse made from him is Eve.
rows.anchor: من المقصود بالنفس الواحدة؟ آدم عليه السلام

words: وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ الْأَنْعَامِ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought Adam and Eve down to earth with the livestock pairs as provisions and necessities for life there, so they were not sent down without food.
rows.anchor: أنزلهما إلى الأرض وأنزل معهما طعامهما مستلزمات الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive creation in mothers’ wombs refers to Adam and Eve’s descendants, not the first couple, whose creation was mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: هذا ليس آدم وحواء وإنما نحن وذكر خلق آدم وحواء في بداية السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nahl first speaks of humanity’s creation and then livestock created for people; al-Zumar first mentions Adam and Eve, then their descendants and provisions.
rows.anchor: هذا خلقنا نحن وليس آدم ثم ذكر بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending down a visible parchment is more striking than sending an angel, so the verse uses nazzalnā for the parchment and anzalnā for the angel.
rows.anchor: تنزيل القرطاس أهمّ وآكد وأغرب من تنزيل الملك لذا قال نزّلنا وأنزلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “أنزلناه وبالحق نزل,” anzala is transitive while nazala is intransitive, describing descent of itself; this difference is not one of rank.
rows.anchor: أنزل فعل متعدي ونزل فعل لازم (نزل من تلقاء نفسه)

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Some distinguish anzala as a one-time descent and nazzala as gradual revelation; grammarians object that the Quran itself uses nazzala for a single, complete descent.
rows.anchor: قسم يقولون أنزل أي كله جملة واحدة ونزّل منجماً لكن قسم من النحاة ردوا على هذا القول

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Another reported distinction is that anzala is general while nazzala is specific.
rows.anchor: وقسم قالوا أنزل عام ونزّل خاص

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: A further account says the Quran was sent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven all at once, then revealed gradually; “أنزلناه” in the Night of Decree is read this way.
rows.anchor: أنزل من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا دفعة واحدة

rows.speaker: القدماء
rows.claim: Early scholars noticed that surahs opening with a disconnected letter often contain many words featuring that letter, as in Qaf and Sad.
rows.anchor: تتكرر فيها الكلمات التي فيها حرف القاف مثل (قول، رقيب، القرآن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes that the fourteen opening letters form half the alphabet and are represented across twenty-nine surahs, while balancing halves of several phonetic categories.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: لو نظرنا في عدد الحروف (14) حرفاً تمثّل نصف حروف المعجم

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: One group takes the letters in Alif Lam Mim to represent the beginning, middle, and end of creation, respectively.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال أنه تشتمل على أنصاف الأحرف مثلاً كل سورة بدأت بـ (ألم)

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Another group observes that every surah beginning with Ṭā starts by telling the story of Moses.
rows.anchor: وقسم قالوا أن كل السور التي تبدأ بحرف (ط) تبدأ بقصة موسى أولاً

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: One proposed mathematical pattern equates the ratio of Alif to Lam occurrences with the ratio of Lam to Mim occurrences in surahs beginning Alif Lam Mim.
rows.anchor: أن كل سورة فيها (ألم) نسبة الحروف ألف إلى لام تساوي نسبة الحروف لام إلى ميم

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Other approaches turn the letters into phrases, assign them to groups, or treat them as symbols for future events; Ibn Kathir reports an allusion in Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf to events involving the Prophet’s family, and some use abjad values such as alif equals one.
rows.anchor: وقسم يجمع الحروف في جمل وقسم أجروها على الطوائف فجعلوا من الأحرف الأربعة عشر جملاً متعددة

rows.speaker: الكثيرون
rows.claim: The widespread view is that the Quran uses the same letters people speak, yet produces inimitable speech and challenges them to match it.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه الكثيرين أن القرآن مؤلف من أجناس هذه الأحرف التي تتحدثون بها وجاء بكلام معجز

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: The early Muslim authorities entrusted the meanings of the disconnected letters to God.
rows.anchor: والسلف كانوا يوكلون معاني هذه الأحرف لله تعالى

rows.speaker: القدامى
rows.claim: One famous early interpretation is that Muslim conquests gradually annex lands of unbelief to the realm of Islam.
rows.anchor: أن نأتي البلاد (بلاد الكفر) نفتحها شيئاً فشيئاً ونلحقها بدار الإسلام

rows.speaker: القدامى
rows.claim: A second early interpretation is that the earth loses its scholars, expressed by the saying that a region dies when its scholar dies.
rows.anchor: والآخر موت العلماء (علماء الإسلام) الأرض تحيا إذا ما عاش عالمها إن يمت عالم مات طرف

rows.speaker: المحدثين
rows.claim: One modern reading calls the phrase a scientific sign: the earth is egg-shaped, with its ends shorter than its middle.
rows.anchor: الأول أن فيها إعجاز علمي أنها كروية بيضية ننقصها من أطرافها

rows.speaker: المحدثين
rows.claim: Another modern reading says the earth continually shrinks as gases escape and evaporate, reducing its size from the inside.
rows.anchor: والآخر أنها تنقص باستمرار تنكمش الأرض ويقل حجمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He favors the conquest reading in context: the parallel verse asks whether people are victorious, and victory is associated with Islam.
rows.anchor: معناها التوجيه الأول أنه فتحها وألحقها بدار الإسلام، وفي موضع آخر قال تعالى (فهم الغالبون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divine injunction to honor parents removes suspicion that Luqman advises his son for personal benefit; God has no such self-interest.
rows.anchor: الموصي هو الله وليست له فيه مصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form waṣṣā is used for weighty religious and moral matters, while awṣā is used for material matters such as inheritance.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى يقول (وصّى) بالتشديد إذا كان أمر الوصية شديداً ومهماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes one Quranic exception where awṣā concerns religion: Jesus says he was enjoined to pray and give alms, while still an infant and not legally responsible.
rows.anchor: لم ترد في القرآن أوصى في أمور الدين إلا في مكان واحد اقترنت بالأمور المادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “We enjoined” attributes the important good injunction to God Himself.
rows.anchor: قال وصّى وأسند الوصية إلى ضمير التعظيم (ووصينا) والله تعالى ينسب الأمور إلى نفسه في الأمور المهمة وأمور الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse chooses “بوالديه” rather than “بأبويه.”
rows.anchor: ولم يقل بأبويه بل اختار بوالديه
